label: STOPP L6
title: Paracetamol at 3 g a day or more with low body weight or liver disease
statement: Paracetamol at doses ≥ 3 g/24 hours in patients with poor nutritional status i.e., BMI < 18 or chronic liver disease (risk of hepatotoxicity).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: Taking 3 g or more of paracetamol in a day raises the risk of liver damage in a person who is underweight (BMI under 18) or has long-term liver disease.

medicine_groups.name: Paracetamol, alone or in combination

paracetamol: Lemsip Cold and Flu Liquid Capsule
Panadol Back and Neck Long Lasting
Panadol Back and Neck Pain Relief
Panadol Children's Drops 1 Month to 2 Years
Tylenol for Babies 1 Month to 2 Years

medicine_groups.note: Paracetamol in combination products counts towards the daily total. Panadeine is paracetamol with codeine. Mersyndol is paracetamol with codeine and doxylamine. Maxigesic is paracetamol with ibuprofen. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Count only the paracetamol in the identified product. A line that says only Codral does not establish the ingredients or their amounts.

needs_facts.meets: Enter the measured BMI in kg/m2 and its measurement date if known. A BMI below 18 kg/m2 meets the nutritional risk threshold.

needs_facts.what: Chronic liver disease (for example cirrhosis or chronic hepatitis)

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only to people aged 65 years or older. If age is unknown and the other conditions are met, report only a possible finding and ask for the age. First check the total paracetamol dose in 24 hours. The total is worked out from the paracetamol amount per unit times units per dose, or the concentration in mg/mL times mL per dose, multiplied by doses per 24 hours and summed across concurrent products. For as-needed directions, distinguish the permitted maximum from documented use. If the as-needed maximum is below 3,000 mg across all products, return no finding. If both risk factors are ruled out, return no finding. If actual intake is unclear and could reach 3,000 mg, report a possible finding. Cite the supplies and name the missing value "Paracetamol daily dose actually taken in mg". A known total below 3,000 mg gives no L6 finding regardless of BMI or liver history. At 3,000 mg or more, suspect a finding if BMI is below 18 or chronic liver disease is documented. Cite the Group A paracetamol supplies and the qualifying fact. If the dose reaches or could reach 3,000 mg and neither risk factor is established, report a possible finding when either risk factor is unknown. Cite the supplies and name each missing risk factor as "BMI" or "Chronic liver disease (for example cirrhosis or chronic hepatitis)", as applicable. A normal ALT does not rule out chronic liver disease. Return no finding on risk grounds only when BMI is at least 18 and the history explicitly rules out chronic liver disease.
cannot_be_seen: The person's weight or BMI, any liver disease, alcohol use, and how much paracetamol is really taken. Also paracetamol bought without a prescription or supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: The person's nutritional status and liver health, and whether a lower daily paracetamol dose or another pain plan would be safer.
